report.source_text: After treatment with intravenous heparin and a 6-month course of coumarin, CVT resolved completely. At the 3-year follow-up at the Department of Neurology, the patient had no complaints, her neurological examination was unremarkable, and her visual acuity was intact.

clinician.final_diagnosis: venous stroke due to homozygous Factor V Leiden mutation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old girl from a consanguineous family presented with a 4-month history of worsening chronic holocranial headache and visual blurring. On admission, examination revealed bilateral papilledema and reduced visual acuity; neurological exam was otherwise unremarkable. MRI with gadolinium confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis with a linear filling defect in the superior sagittal sinus. Laboratory hypercoagulability workup was notable for elevated D-dimers with normal protein C, protein S, and antithrombin levels. Genetic testing demonstrated a unique homozygous Factor V Leiden mutation. The patient was treated with intravenous heparin followed by 6 months of coumarin anticoagulation. Complete resolution of CVT occurred, and at 3-year follow-up, she was neurologically normal with intact vision.
